standard_prerequisites.name: Minimal models, minimal numerical types and exceptional curves of the first kind
standard_prerequisites.statement: In the regular-model situation the numerical type attached to the model records the multiplicities, the genus of each component, the intersection numbers of pairs of components and the residue field degrees; the type is called minimal when no index has both genus zero and self-intersection equal to the negative of the residue field degree, and a curve is called exceptional of the first kind when it is a smooth rational curve with self-intersection minus one over its field of definition. The author's own definitions are the allowed inputs, stated in the same section and in the Algebraic Curves chapter.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the bridge between the geometric notion of a minimal model and the combinatorial notion of a minimal numerical type, and it is used whenever the chapter switches between the two.

core_obligations: One direction: if the numerical type is minimal then no component has genus zero with self-intersection equal to the negative of its residue field degree, so none of the components is an exceptional curve of the first kind and the model has nothing to contract (source lines 5287-5290).

The other direction: if the type is not minimal, pick an index witnessing it, that is a component of genus zero whose self-intersection is the negative of the residue field degree, and show that this component is exceptional of the first kind (source lines 5293-5295).

Compute the degree: the restriction of the invertible sheaf attached to the negative of that component has degree equal to the residue field degree when the component is viewed over the residue field, hence degree one when it is viewed over its own field of definition (source lines 5295-5300).

Identify the component as a projective line over its field of definition using the quoted classification of curves of degree one, then use that the Picard group of the projective line over a field is the integers to see that the normal sheaf of the component is the twist by minus one, which is the defining property of an exceptional curve of the first kind (source lines 5300-5309).

proof_roadmap.step: Minimal type implies no component is exceptional of the first kind.
Non-minimal type provides a component of genus zero whose self-intersection is minus the residue field degree.
Degree computation for the restriction of the sheaf attached to the negative of the component.
Identify the component with a projective line and read off the normal sheaf, which makes it exceptional of the first kind.
